items.title: Louis Armstrong Interview, 1971-07-09
items.q: Fred Robbins, a jazz critic, was the last person outside the family who saw the King of Jazz last Sunday on his 71st birthday.

ctx.x: Just a closer walk with thee. Just a closer walk with thee. Granted, Jesus, if you please. Granted, Jesus, if you please. Dear Lord, let it be. Dear Lord, let it be. Dear Lord, let it be. Let it be. Dear Lord, let it be. Dear Lord, let it be. I am weak, but thou art strong. I am weak, but thou art strong. I am weak, but thou art strong. Jesus, keep me from all wrong. Jesus, keep me from all wrong. I'll be satisfied. I am weak, but thou art strong. Lord, as long as I want. Let me walk, let me walk close to thee.…

Fred Robbins, a jazz critic, was the last person outside the family who saw the King of Jazz last Sunday on his 71st birthday. Robbins talked about the man and his music. Alas, poor world. What treasure thou hast lost. Whom the gods love die young, no matter how long they live. One of the world's greatest men is gone. One of the last of the true giants. Who is an artist of such extraordinary ability that he is above all possible praise. And he is a great honor for me to pay him homage to these few words. He…
